narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated an 84% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—a high risk signal that the school chose not to accept. Among the factors that most influenced this decision, your third-year class rank mattered most: at the lowest decile, you were far below the typical accepted student around the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your LSAT score was the second most influential factor; a score of 20 is well below the accepted-student average of about 37 and also pushed toward failure. The third most important factor, your first-year rank, was closer to the accepted average (5 versus about 6) and actually leaned toward passing, but it was not strong enough to offset the other two signals. Your gender and race were not used in the prediction. To move forward, ask admissions whether the decision can be reconsidered or appealed and what evidence would help, such as updated grades or a stronger test score. Then focus on improving your LSAT through structured preparation and, if possible, strengthen your academic record before reapplying; also seek pre-law advising to target schools where your profile is a better fit.
